data.gender_notes: Musaraf is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who invokes the rain, often considered a god or goddess of fertility and agriculture. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Musaraf usually hope their child will grow to embody bringer of rain and live with faith, good character and purpose.

The name "Musaraf" thus evokes a sense of respect and reverence for the natural elements and their role in sustaining life.

historical_references.reference: Musaraf was a ruler in the northern Indian kingdom of Kashmir, reigning from 1394 to 1410 CE. He is known for his patronage of arts and architecture, particularly the construction of the Hazratbal Mosque and the Shankaracharya Temple.

Musaraf Shah Sur was a Sultan of the Bengal Sultanate, ruling from 1533 to 1538 CE. He is known for his military campaigns against the Mughal Empire and the establishment of the Adil Shah Dynasty, which lasted until 1686 CE.
